result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder rules in `addTestConventions` in `ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394). A folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is.

- **Before:** `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+/.*` and `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+/.*`. These needed at least one extra ASCII character after `mock`, so a plain `mock/` folder was missed. Punctuation and non-ASCII characters in the name also stopped the match.
- **After:** `.*/mock[^/\\\\]*/.*` and `.*/__mock[^/\\\\]*/.*`. The rest of the name can be anything except a path separator, so the match stays inside one folder name.

Backslash paths already work because `SourceFileFilter.matches` also tries the path with separators normalized.

I ran the module's scoping and convention tests and they passed. I did not add tests for the new cases, and I did not run the specific paths from your list (`mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/`, `mock模拟/`, `remock/`, `demo/`, `mock.java`).
